title.en: Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change

chapterTag.category: AP Calc AB Unit 6 — Integration & Accumulation

body.en: Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change covers essential College Board AP Calculus AB competencies across foundational mechanics, intermediate analysis, and advanced FRQ problem solving.

blocks.heading: Level 1 · Foundations — Riemann Sums & Definite Integrals

body.en: Approximate areas using Left, Right, Midpoint, and Trapezoidal sums. Definite integral \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx\) represents signed net area.

Part 1 (Accumulation): \(\frac{d}{dx}\left[\int_a^x f(t)\,dt\right] = f(x)\).
Part 2 (Evaluation): \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a)\) where \(F'(x) = f(x)\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

A function \(f(x)\) has table values: \(f(0)=2, f(2)=5, f(4)=9\). Approximate \(\int_0^4 f(x)\,dx\) using the Trapezoidal Rule with 2 subintervals of equal width.

solution.en: Subinterval width \(\Delta x = 2\). Trapezoidal formula: \[ T = \frac{\Delta x}{2} [f(0) + 2f(2) + f(4)] = \frac{2}{2} [2 + 2(5) + 9] = 2 + 10 + 9 = \mathbf{21}. \]

blocks.heading: Level 2 · Medium — Fundamental Theorem of Calculus & u-Substitution

body.en: Evaluate definite integrals analytically via antiderivatives and apply u-substitution with adjusted limits of integration.

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

Evaluate the definite integral \(\int_0^2 2x e^{x^2}\,dx\).

solution.en: Let \(u = x^2 \implies du = 2x\,dx\). When \(x = 0\), \(u = 0\); when \(x = 2\), \(u = 4\). \[ \int_0^4 e^u\,du = \left[ e^u \right]_0^4 = e^4 - e^0 = \mathbf{e^4 - 1} \approx 53.598. \]

blocks.heading: Level 3 · Advanced — Accumulation Functions & Chain Rule with Integrals

body.en: Differentiate variable-limit accumulation functions: \(\frac{d}{dx}\left[\int_a^{g(x)} f(t)\,dt\right] = f(g(x)) \cdot g'(x)\).

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

Find \(g'(x)\) for the function \(g(x) = \int_1^{x^3} \sqrt{t^2 + 7}\,dt\).

solution.en: Apply FTC Part 1 with the Chain Rule: \[ g'(x) = \sqrt{(x^3)^2 + 7} \cdot \frac{d}{dx}[x^3] = \mathbf{3x^2\sqrt{x^6 + 7}}. \]
